reports.title: Epstein Files News: Lawmakers Demand Vote | 3 Million+ Files Still Hidden? | US News | N18G
reports.description:
The political battle over the Jeffrey Epstein files is back in the spotlight in Washington, with lawmakers pushing for another vote aimed at forcing greater transparency and disclosure.

Republican Rep. Thomas Massie and Democratic Reps. Ro Khanna and Teresa Leger Fernández are leading a new effort to compel a House vote through a discharge petition. The initiative comes after lawmakers argued that millions of Epstein-related records remain undisclosed despite the earlier transparency legislation.

The new petition needs 218 House signatures to force the measure onto the floor. As of September 1, it had gathered 17 signatures, including Massie and several Democratic lawmakers.

The push is also reviving questions over what remains in the government’s possession, what can legally be released, and how victim privacy and ongoing investigations should be protected. Lawmakers are demanding greater accountability while the Justice Department faces renewed scrutiny over its handling of the files.

The political stakes are high, with the Epstein scandal continuing to generate pressure across party lines. The latest congressional push also comes amid renewed attention to people named in Epstein-related documents; being named or associated in records does not by itself establish criminal wrongdoing.
